answers.question: Which product categories bring in the most revenue?
answers.sql: SELECT category, total_revenue, total_orders FROM warehouse.vw_product_customer_affinity ORDER BY total_revenue DESC, category ASC LIMIT 10
answers.measure_used: total_revenue (price + freight, delivered orders, BRL) from vw_product_customer_affinity
assumptions: Revenue is measured in BRL and includes both product price and freight value.
The default limit of 10 was applied to show the top categories.
The main alternative is product-only revenue (excluding freight), which is available via total_product_revenue.
follow_ups: What is the repeat purchase rate for these top product categories?
What is the average review score for these top product categories?

explanation.headline: The health_beauty category brings in the most revenue, generating BRL 1.41 million across 8,647 delivered orders.
explanation.text: Revenue is measured as the sum of product price and freight value for delivered orders. Among the top 10 categories shown, health_beauty leads with BRL 1.41 million, followed closely by watches_gifts at BRL 1.26 million and bed_bath_table at BRL 1.23 million. The lowest-earning category in this top group is garden_tools, which brought in BRL 567,146 across 3,448 orders.
caveats: Revenue includes both product price and freight value.
The results are limited to the top 10 categories by revenue and do not represent marketplace-wide totals.
An alternative measure is product-only revenue, which excludes freight costs.

answers.question: Which states have the most revenue?
answers.sql: SELECT state, total_revenue, total_orders, revenue_share_pct FROM warehouse.vw_regional_analysis ORDER BY total_revenue DESC, state ASC LIMIT 10
answers.measure_used: total_revenue (price + freight, delivered orders, BRL) from vw_regional_analysis
assumptions: Used customer state (demand-side) as the default region definition; seller state (supply-side) is the main alternative.
Revenue includes both product price and freight value for delivered orders in BRL.
follow_ups: Which states have the highest average order value?
What is the average delivery time for each of these states?

explanation.headline: São Paulo (SP) is the leading state by revenue, generating BRL 5.77 million, which represents 37.4% of the marketplace total.
explanation.text: This analysis measures total revenue, which includes product price and freight value for delivered orders, grouped by the customer's state. Among the 10 states shown, São Paulo (SP) leads with BRL 5.77 million from 40,501 orders, followed by Rio de Janeiro (RJ) with BRL 2.06 million and Minas Gerais (MG) with BRL 1.82 million. There is a clear gap between these top three states and the rest, as fourth-place Rio Grande do Sul (RS) drops to BRL 861,473. Espírito Santo (ES) has the lowest revenue among the group at BRL 317,658.
caveats: This analysis uses the customer's state to define the region, whereas the seller's state is the main alternative.
Revenue figures are based only on delivered orders.

explanation.headline: Among the top ten states by revenue, São Paulo has the fastest delivery at 8.30 days, while Bahia has the slowest at 18.90 days.
explanation.text: This analysis measures average delivery days and on-time rates for delivered orders across the top ten states by revenue. São Paulo leads with the shortest delivery time of 8.30 days and a high on-time rate of 94.11%. In contrast, Bahia has the longest average delivery time of 18.90 days and the lowest on-time rate at 85.96%. explanation.headline: Among sellers with at least 50 delivered orders, there is no clear relationship between revenue and on-time delivery rates.

Individual on-time rates vary widely from 69.9% to 100.0% across the entire group, with a median of 93.2%. The highest-earning seller, 4869f7a5…, generated BRL 247,007.06 with an 88.4% on-time rate.

answers.question: How many customers are in each RFM segment?
answers.sql:
SELECT segment, COUNT(customer_unique_id) AS customer_count FROM warehouse.vw_rfm GROUP BY segment ORDER BY customer_count DESC, segment
LIMIT 500
answers.measure_used: customer_count (count of distinct customer_unique_id) from vw_rfm
assumptions: Used vw_rfm as the canonical source for RFM segment counts.
Most customers have placed a single order, so frequency-based labels such as Loyal don't necessarily mean repeat purchases.
follow_ups: What is the average order value and total spend for each RFM segment?

explanation.headline: The Loyal segment is the largest with 26,165 customers, while the Recent segment is the smallest with 3,722 customers.
explanation.text: This analysis counts distinct customers across nine RFM segments. The Loyal segment leads with 26,165 customers, followed by About to Sleep with 15,004 customers. Potential Loyal and Need Attention have very similar counts at 11,256 and 11,204 customers respectively. The smallest groups are Champions with 3,784 customers and Recent with 3,722 customers.
caveats: Most customers have placed a single order, so frequency-based labels such as Loyal do not necessarily mean repeat purchases.

answers.question: How does revenue for the top 10 categories vary by month in 2017?
answers.sql:
WITH top_categories AS (SELECT COALESCE(p.product_category_name_english, 'uncategorised') AS category, SUM(f.price + f.freight_value) AS total_revenue FROM warehouse.fact_order_items f JOIN warehouse.dim_product p ON f.product_key = p.product_key JOIN warehouse.dim_order o ON f.order_key = o.order_key JOIN warehouse.dim_date d ON o.purchase_date_key = d.date_key WHERE o.order_status = 'delivered' AND d.year = 2017 GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY total_revenue DESC LIMIT 10) SELECT d.month AS order_month_num, d.month_name AS order_month, COALESCE(p.product_category_name_english, 'uncategorised') AS category, ROUND(SUM(f.price + f.freight_value), 2) AS monthly_revenue, COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS delivered_orders FROM warehouse.fact_order_items f JOIN warehouse.dim_product p ON f.product_key = p.product_key JOIN warehouse.dim_order o ON f.order_key = o.order_key JOIN warehouse.dim_date d ON o.purchase_date_key = d.date_key WHERE o.order_status = 'delivered' AND d.year = 2017 AND COALESCE(p.product_category_name_english, 'uncategorised') IN (SELECT category FROM top_categories) GROUP BY 1, 2, 3 ORDER BY d.month ASC, monthly_revenue DESC
LIMIT 500
answers.measure_used: monthly_revenue (sum of price + freight_value for delivered orders, BRL) and delivered_orders (count of distinct orders) grouped by category and month in 2017
assumptions: No analytical view combines both product category and monthly/temporal grains, so we fall back to joining raw tables (fact_order_items, dim_product, dim_order, dim_date).
Top 10 categories are defined by highest total revenue (price + freight) specifically within the year 2017; the alternative is defining them by overall dataset revenue.
Revenue includes both product price and freight value, in BRL, for delivered orders only.
Products with missing categories are grouped as 'uncategorised' per the platform convention.
follow_ups: What is the repeat purchase rate for each of these product categories?
How does the average delivery time compare across these product categories?

explanation.headline: In 2017, monthly revenue for the top 10 categories peaked in November at BRL 759,379.30, driven by bed_bath_table which reached BRL 104,963.58 that month.
explanation.text: We measured monthly revenue, including price and freight for delivered orders, across the top 10 categories of 2017. Combined revenue for these categories rose from BRL 82,360.09 in January to a peak of BRL 759,379.30 in November. Bed_bath_table led overall category revenue at BRL 580,949.20, while housewares was the lowest of the ten at BRL 275,188.71. November was the strongest month for nine of the ten categories, led by bed_bath_table at BRL 104,963.58 and watches_gifts at BRL 103,135.30.
caveats: Top 10 categories are defined by highest total revenue specifically within the year 2017, rather than overall dataset revenue.
Products with missing categories are grouped as 'uncategorised'.

answers.question: What share of our customers buy more than once?
answers.sql:
SELECT COUNT(CASE WHEN order_count >= 2 THEN 1 END) AS repeat_customers, COUNT(*) AS total_customers, ROUND(COUNT(CASE WHEN order_count >= 2 THEN 1 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(*), 2) AS repeat_purchase_rate_pct FROM warehouse.vw_rfm
LIMIT 500
answers.measure_used: repeat_purchase_rate_pct (percentage of customer_unique_ids with order_count >= 2 in delivered orders from vw_rfm)
assumptions: Customers are identified by customer_unique_id, and only delivered orders are counted, following the default marketplace conventions.
A repeat customer is defined as having 2 or more delivered orders.
We assume the entire historical dataset (Sep 2016 to Aug 2018) is the basis for this calculation.
Caveat: Most customers in this marketplace buy only once, so a low repeat purchase rate is normal and expected.
follow_ups: Which product categories have the highest repeat purchase rates?
How does customer retention develop over time for our monthly cohorts?

explanation.headline: Only 3.0% of our customers have bought more than once on the marketplace.
explanation.text: Out of 93,358 total customers with delivered orders, only 2,801 are repeat customers who made two or more purchases. This measure is based on unique customer identifiers across all delivered orders in the historical dataset from September 2016 to August 2018. The data shows a very large gap between one-time buyers and repeat buyers.
caveats: Most customers in this marketplace buy only once, so a low repeat purchase rate is normal and expected.

answers.question: Do late deliveries get worse reviews than on-time ones?
answers.sql:
SELECT dimension_value AS delivery_status, total_orders, avg_review_score FROM warehouse.vw_delivery_experience WHERE dimension = 'On-time vs Late' ORDER BY avg_review_score DESC
LIMIT 500
answers.measure_used: avg_review_score (average star rating 1-5, order-level) and total_orders from vw_delivery_experience
assumptions: Used vw_delivery_experience filtered to 'On-time vs Late' as the canonical source for comparing delivery performance and satisfaction.
The result shows an association between delivery performance and review scores, not proof of cause.
Any group with fewer than 30 orders should be treated as a small sample where averages can swing on a few orders.
follow_ups: How do on-time and late review scores compare across different Brazilian states?
How does the customer response time to review surveys vary by review score?

explanation.headline: Late deliveries receive much lower reviews, averaging a 2.57 star rating compared to 4.29 stars for on-time deliveries.
explanation.text: The analysis compared average order-level review scores across 88,644 on-time orders and 7,826 late orders. On-time deliveries achieved a high average rating of 4.29 stars. In contrast, late deliveries saw a steep drop in customer satisfaction, averaging only 2.57 stars. This reveals a clear gap in customer satisfaction based on delivery performance.
caveats: The result shows an association between delivery performance and review scores, not proof of cause.

answers.question: Do customers who pay in instalments spend more per order?
answers.sql:
SELECT dimension_value AS instalment_band, order_count, avg_payment_value, avg_order_item_total FROM warehouse.vw_payment_behaviour WHERE dimension = 'By Instalment Band' ORDER BY CASE dimension_value WHEN '1 (Single)' THEN 1 WHEN '2-3' THEN 2 WHEN '4-6' THEN 3 WHEN '7-12' THEN 4 WHEN '12+' THEN 5 ELSE 6 END
LIMIT 500
answers.measure_used: avg_payment_value and avg_order_item_total by instalment band from vw_payment_behaviour
assumptions: Used vw_payment_behaviour filtered to 'By Instalment Band' to compare order values across different instalment counts.
The result shows an association between instalment usage and order value, not proof of cause.
Order values are reported in BRL.
Check order_count to ensure each instalment band has a reliable sample size (under 30 orders can swing easily).
follow_ups: What is the average number of instalments and revenue share for each payment type?
Which product categories have the highest average review scores and order volumes?

explanation.headline: Customers who pay in more instalments spend more per order, with average order values rising from BRL 120.24 for single payments to BRL 414.31 for 12 or more instalments.
explanation.text: The analysis uses average payment value and average order item total across different instalment bands. There is a clear upward trend: single-payment orders average BRL 120.24, while orders with 2-3 instalments average BRL 135.42, and those with 7-12 instalments reach BRL 332.71. The highest average order value of BRL 414.31 is found in the 12+ instalment band. In all bands, the average payment value matches the average order item total exactly.
caveats: The result shows an association between instalment usage and order value, not proof of cause.

answers.sql:
SELECT order_month, total_revenue, total_revenue_mom_growth_pct, total_orders FROM warehouse.vw_new_vs_returning_revenue WHERE order_month >= '2017-01-01' ORDER BY order_month ASC
LIMIT 500
answers.measure_used: total_revenue (price + freight, delivered orders, BRL) from vw_new_vs_returning_revenue
assumptions: Used vw_new_vs_returning_revenue as the canonical source for monthly marketplace performance
Revenue includes both product price and freight value for delivered orders, measured in BRL
Filtered from January 2017 onwards, which excludes the very thin transaction volume of late 2016
follow_ups: What share of monthly revenue is driven by returning customers over this same period?

explanation.headline: Monthly marketplace revenue grew from BRL 127,482 in January 2017 to BRL 985,492 in August 2018, peaking at BRL 1.15 million in November 2017.
explanation.text: This analysis tracks monthly total revenue, which includes product prices and freight values for delivered orders. Revenue rose overall but experienced several notable dips, such as a drop to BRL 843,078 in December 2017 following the November peak, and a decline to BRL 966,168 in February 2018. After recovering to BRL 1.13 million in April 2018, revenue trended slightly downward to BRL 985,492 by August 2018. Total monthly orders followed a similar trajectory, starting at 750 orders and peaking at 7,289 orders in November 2017.
